text: We evaluated a learned noisy-channel model of weak-label errors refined by expectation-maximization, using 3 EM rounds, with pythia-410m as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-3b as the strong student, across num_seeds = 2 seeds. The weak model reached 0.52 accuracy and the strong ceiling was 0.78, while the weak-to-strong transfer accuracy was 0.58 with a standard error of 0.01. The resulting performance gap recovered (PGR) was 0.22 with a standard error of 0.05, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.25. The method therefore does not recover more of the gap than the baseline; the observed PGR sits below it, and with a standard error of 0.05 the two values are not separated by more than two standard errors, so no directional conclusion is warranted either way. With only two seeds, these estimates are preliminary and the variance is poorly characterized; additional seeds would be needed before drawing inferences about the channel model's effect.
